heard: A tiny frozen moon is painting one of Saturn's rings. Enceladus is only 310 miles wide, yet it is the most reflective body in the solar system. Because its pristine surface bounces back almost all sunlight, temperatures hover around minus 324 degrees Fahrenheit. For over two centuries, astronomers had no idea how such a small rock stayed dazzlingly white. Then in 2005, The Cassini spacecraft caught giant fractures dubbed tiger stripes erupting near its south pole. Massive geysers blast water vapor, salts, and organic molecules straight into space. Measuring the moon's subtle orbital wobble revealed that these jets tap directly into a global liquid ocean. Much of this ocean spray falls back as pristine snow, while the rest escapes to build Saturn's E-ring.
